rubric.why: Identifies heat capacity as the heat supplied to a body.
rubric.description: States that heat capacity is the amount of heat required for a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the heat required by the body.

rubric.why: Includes the defining unit temperature rise.
rubric.description: Specifies a temperature rise of one degree Celsius or one kelvin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the temperature rises by one unit.

modelAnswer: Heat capacity is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a body by 1°C (or 1 K).

items.followUp: Write four differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Distinguishes mass from weight by their physical meanings.
rubric.description: Mass is the amount of matter in a body; weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing their meanings.

rubric.why: States that mass does not depend on location.
rubric.description: Mass remains constant from place to place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mass is independent of location.

rubric.why: States that weight depends on the gravitational field.
rubric.description: Weight varies with the strength of gravity and location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that weight changes with gravity or location.

rubric.why: Gives the standard units and measuring instruments.
rubric.description: Mass is measured in kilograms using a beam/physical balance; weight is measured in newtons using a spring balance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit-and-instrument distinction.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, while weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
Mass remains constant at different places, while weight varies with the strength of gravity.
The SI unit of mass is the kilogram (kg), while the SI unit of weight is the newton (N).
Mass is measured with a beam balance, while weight is measured with a spring balance.

items.followUp: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m s⁻² over a distance of 25 m. Find its speed in km h⁻¹.

rubric.why: Records the given values in SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies initial speed, acceleration and distance correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given data.

rubric.why: Uses the appropriate equation of motion.
rubric.description: Selects the relation connecting speed, acceleration and distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

rubric.why: Substitutes the values and obtains the speed in SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes correctly and obtains 10 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and calculation.

rubric.why: Gives the speed before conversion with its unit.
rubric.description: States the speed as 10 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct intermediate speed and unit.

rubric.why: Converts the speed to the requested unit.
rubric.description: Gives the final speed as 36 km h⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m s⁻¹, a = 0.5 m s⁻², s = 100 m.
Using v² = u² + 2as:
v = 10 m s⁻¹.
Converting to km h⁻¹: 10 × 3.6 = 36 km h⁻¹.
Answer: The train's speed is 36 km h⁻¹.

items.followUp: A force of 80 N acts at an angle of 60° to the X-axis. Find its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: Identifies the force and its angle to the X-axis.
rubric.description: Records the given force and angle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Uses the correct component relations for an angle measured from the X-axis.
rubric.description: States the horizontal and vertical component formulae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct component formulae.

rubric.why: Calculates the X-component correctly.
rubric.description: Finds the X-component as approximately 43.3 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct X-component and unit.

rubric.why: Calculates the Y-component correctly.
rubric.description: Finds the Y-component as 25 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct Y-component and unit.

rubric.why: Reports both perpendicular components with units.
rubric.description: States the final pair of perpendicular components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly identifying both final components.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N and θ = 30°.
The perpendicular components are Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ.
Answer: The X-component is 43.3 N and the Y-component is 25 N.

items.followUp: A force of 40 N makes an angle of 60° with the X-axis. Find its X- and Y-components.

rubric.why: Converts the square's side to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the side length from millimetres to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI conversion.

rubric.why: Finds the area of the square face.
rubric.description: Calculates the area as 1 × 10⁻⁴ m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area with unit.

rubric.why: Uses the definition of pressure.
rubric.description: States the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the force and area and evaluates the quotient.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given force and calculated area correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and calculation.

rubric.why: Gives the pressure with the SI unit.
rubric.description: States the final pressure as 2 × 10⁵ Pa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 10 mm = 0.01 m, F = 20 N.
Area of the square head: A = (0.01 m)² = 0.0001 m².
Pressure: P = F/A.
Answer: The pressure is 2 × 10⁵ Pa.

rubric.why: Defines plasma physics by its subject matter.
rubric.description: States that plasma physics studies plasma, an ionized gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of plasma physics.

rubric.why: Defines geophysics by its subject matter.
rubric.description: States that geophysics studies the physical properties or processes of the Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of geophysics.

modelAnswer: Plasma physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, an ionized gas.
Geophysics is the branch of physics that studies the physical properties and processes of the Earth.

items.followUp: State one difference between a beam balance and a spring balance.

rubric.why: Describes how an electronic balance measures and presents the result.
rubric.description: States that an electronic balance measures mass electronically and displays the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the electronic measurement/display feature.

rubric.why: Describes the comparative, mechanical operation of a physical balance.
rubric.description: States that a physical balance compares an unknown mass with standard masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct operation of a physical balance.

modelAnswer: An electronic balance measures mass electronically and shows the result on a digital display.
A physical balance measures mass by comparing the object with standard masses using a mechanical balance.

items.followUp: How is a laboratory stopwatch used to measure the time of an event?

rubric.why: Describes timing the beginning and end of the interval.
rubric.description: Starts the stopwatch at the beginning of the event and stops it at the end.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct start-and-stop procedure.

rubric.why: Explains how to obtain the measured time from the stopwatch.
rubric.description: Reads the elapsed time from the digital display; the stopwatch can be reset to zero before another measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for reading the display or correctly describing the reset.

modelAnswer: Press the start button at the beginning of the event and the stop button at its end.
Read the elapsed time on the digital display; press reset to return the stopwatch to zero before the next measurement.
